items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 55:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the external Partzuf of Aba and Ima? The aspect of Aba and Ima that is in permanence, which are only in the stature of SAG, and clothe from the throat and below of AA, and have no hold in the head of AA — their stature is then discerned by the name the external Partzuf of Aba and Ima. For they are from their root in Nekudim, the aspect of Hochma and Bina, and they need the GAR of AB, which is the stature of the GAR of AA, of which they now have only the aspect of VAK alone, and every VAK is called externality, as above in Answer 54. And therefore they are called the external Partzuf of Aba and Ima. (Item 178).
